verdict.rationale: CockroachDB's own SQL API lets users manipulate data with statements, and its official MCP server lets AI tools execute statements and insert rows. That supports set-based operations across many rows in principle. The evidence never explicitly documents bulk operations as such, so the depth and extent are unproven. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of bulk insert/update/delete or bulk import features, evidence that bulk statements work through the MCP/agent path, and independent hands-on corroboration of bulk workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: provides a familiar **SQL** API for structuring, manipulating, and querying data
A user can interact with their clusters using natural language prompts to perform read and write operations such as listing tables, executing statements, and inserting rows into a table.
Your AI tools can explore live schemas and run queries against any cluster using OAuth or API key authentication.
